title: Thinking like a Human Biologist: Interpolation and Extrapolation

starterQuestions.q: Convert 350 nm into micrometres (µm) in standard form.
Calculate percentage change if resting heart rate is 65 bpm and peak post-exercise is 143 bpm.
What is the mathematical distinction between interpolation and extrapolation?
starterQuestions.a: Interpolation estimates values within the range of collected data points; extrapolation predicts values beyond the measured experimental boundaries.

starterQuestions.q: Why is extrapolation risky when modelling human physiological recovery curves?
starterQuestions.a: Physiological responses are governed by non-linear homeostatic feedback, enzymatic saturation, and recovery limits, so trends rarely stay linear.

starterQuestions.q: What happens to the Surface Area-to-Volume (SA:V) ratio as cell radius increases?
starterQuestions.a: The SA:V ratio decreases because volume scales with radius cubed (r³) while surface area scales with radius squared (r²).

starterQuestions.q: State the standard metric unit for cardiac frequency.
starterQuestions.a: Beats per minute (bpm) or Hertz (Hz = beats per second).

courseName: OCR Level 3 Cambridge Advanced National (AAQ) in Human Biology

objectives.knowledge: Master core biological mathematical calculations: standard form, unit conversions across 3 orders of magnitude, and SA:V ratios.
objectives.application: Collect live cardiovascular data (resting vs post-exercise heart rate) and construct scientifically rigorous line graphs.
objectives.evaluation: Evaluate the validity of interpolated vs extrapolated clinical predictions, highlighting physiological limits to linear models.

terminology.def: 1 mm = 1,000 µm = 1,000,000 nm. Scale factors are powers of 10³.
Estimating unmeasured intermediate values located strictly within the experimental range of known data points.
Projecting trends beyond the observed data range, carrying high risk of error due to unverified biological assumptions.
